findings.text: For every integer n≥0, the maximum number of connected regions formed by n distinct entire straight lines in the Euclidean plane is 1+n(n+1)/2. For n≥1, the lines y=kx+k², k=1,…,n, attain the maximum; the empty arrangement attains it for n=0.
findings.investigated_claim: For every nonnegative integer n, the greatest possible number of regions is M(n) = 1 + n(n+1)/2. For n ≥ 1, the lines L_k: y = kx + k², k = 1,…,n, attain this bound.
